A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NOICE study. Text, equations, figures, tables and all six appendices are readable and support reliable comparison. Appendix content matches apart from page and table numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on Llama, Gemma, Mistral and GPT-4o, including attack success rates, defense comparisons, scaling analyses and sample outputs.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Claude Haiku results, additional comparator results and empirical measurements of the proposed refusal mechanism.

M1.justification: NOICE dataset construction and the AMD and FRD procedures remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B. Vanilla SFT is an added comparator, not a component of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use HelpSteer and LLM-LAT/harmful-dataset for training and the same 300-prompt HeX-PHI harmful-response evaluation task. The Claude addition extends target model configurations within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 8 adds Vanilla SFT to the Llama, Gemma and Mistral comparisons. Table 5 substantially expands the GPT-4o comparison beyond v1's original-model baseline, adding Vanilla SFT, ISA, YOC and a harmful-data training attempt marked blocked.

E3.justification: v3 adds prefix-controlled probability measurements on Llama-3-8B-Instruct with 5000 training examples for one epoch, and Claude Haiku evaluation with 1000 examples for one epoch. Existing benchmark, evaluator, defense settings and scaling protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Table 2 supplements the existing mechanism analysis with initial-refusal probabilities and harmful-continuation measurements under enforced prefixes. This is a targeted extension on one model; the existing defense, model-size, training-size and appendix case analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing uncertainty values and plotted bands are retained. Neither version specifies seeds, repeated-run counts or uncertainty definitions, and v3 introduces no identified statistical testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports Claude Haiku ASR of 0.72 versus its 0.0133 baseline, GPT-4o comparator ASRs of 0.043 for Vanilla SFT, 0.013 for ISA and 0.06 for YOC, and additional open-model and probability-table results. Existing GPT-4o NOICE ASR of 0.57 and corresponding earlier open-model and appendix scores are retained.

T1.justification: Section 6 retains the same probability decomposition, definitions and assumptions. The added table empirically measures existing quantities; it introduces no new mathematical derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract extends demonstrated closed-source applicability from GPT-4o alone to GPT-4o and Claude Haiku, adding the 72% Haiku claim. The three central contributions and the stated attack and defense mechanisms otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v3 Table 5 newly hypothesizes that stricter moderation of fine-tuned OpenAI models explains comparator ASRs below the original-model baseline. The main mechanism interpretation and Section 9's applicability boundaries and limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: v3 identifies AWS as the Claude fine-tuning route, specifies direct HelpSteer training for Vanilla SFT, and provides the sample count and epoch setting for the probability experiment. The evaluator prompt, NOICE construction algorithm and training examples in Appendices A–C remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands coverage of fine-tuning attacks, post-training safety evaluation and safety realignment, including VIRUS, No Two Devils Alike and Antidote. Section 10 explicitly acknowledges other inference-time and realignment alternatives when positioning the defense, extending the earlier research context beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: a Vanilla SFT subsection, a renamed Section 6, additions to the abstract and related work, an Anthropic disclosure statement, and an author-name refinement. Most prose, section ordering and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the probability and Haiku tables, reformats and expands the GPT-4o table, and inserts a Vanilla SFT row into the open-model table. Figure 4 moves from page 7 to page 8; existing figures and appendix displays are retained with local reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The Vanilla SFT control, direct GPT-4o comparisons and Claude Haiku result strengthen empirical support, while expanded related work improves context. These gains are tempered by a new reporting inconsistency: Section 7.4 still says other attacks were not tested on production models, contradicting Table 5.
